coverage.member: FusionToolbar(#if NET48 this HtmlHelper<TModel> html, #else this IHtmlHelper<TModel> html, #endif ReactivePlan<TModel> plan, string elementId, Action<ToolbarBuilder> build)
coverage.catches: the FusionToolbar render helper stops rendering the command bar bound to its items (the test asserts the toolbar root is visible and shows Pay balance / Request maintenance / Message care team)
the Clicked event selector stops firing when a toolbar command is clicked, so the status banner never appears (the test clicks Request maintenance and asserts the banner reads it)
the .Reactive wiring stops connecting the toolbar's clicked event to its plan pipeline, so clicking a command runs no reaction and the banner stays hidden
the clicked event-arg contract stops delivering the click payload into the plan, so the banner that reads from the payload never updates
FusionToolbarClickedArgs.Item stops carrying the clicked item object, so the Item.Text read yields nothing and the banner text is empty (the test asserts it reads Request maintenance)
FusionToolbarItem.Text stops carrying the clicked command's label (the test asserts the status banner reads exactly Request maintenance after clicking that command)

the FusionToolbarItem payload contract stops carrying per-item identity, so a second distinct command cannot show its own label (the test clicks Message care team and asserts the banner reads exactly that, not the previous command's text)

FusionToolbarItem.Id stops carrying the clicked command's id, so the When(args, x => x.Item.Id).Eq("pay-balance") branch never matches; paying would fall to the Else status branch and the server payment confirmation would never appear (the test asserts the confirmation text)

FusionToolbarItem.Disabled stops riding the gather body; a trusted click only ever lands on an enabled item, so the test asserts the POST carries "commandDisabled":false under its declared key (P025) and fails if the payload mapping breaks

coverage.member: Disable(this ComponentRef<FusionToolbar, TModel> self, bool value)
coverage.catches: Disable stops toggling the toolbar's disabled state (the test asserts the root gains e-disabled after Pay balance and loses it after Done)

acceptedFanout.reason: One user gesture (clicking Request maintenance) with DISTINCT fails-when-broken facts per member, not one assertion claimed for many: the banner appearing at all proves the event delivery cluster (Clicked fires, Reactive wires it, FusionToolbarClickedArgs delivers the payload, FusionToolbarClickedArgs.Item delivers the item object); the banner's exact text 'Request maintenance' proves FusionToolbarItem.Text carries the clicked label. FusionToolbarItem (per-item identity, not a constant) is proven SEPARATELY by messaging_the_care_team_shows_that_action_started asserting a second distinct label. Item.Id, Item.Disabled, Disable, and the render helper are each proven by their own dedicated tests.
